item.title: Canonical LXD and MicroCloud max severity flaw CVE-2026-112816 allows client impersonation and root host access
item.description:
Cloud container and hypervisor infrastructure maintainers have issued out-of-band security updates to resolve a maximum-severity authentication vulnerability in cloud management interfaces. Remote unauthenticated threat actors can bypass cryptographic client authentication controls to hijack cluster resources and obtain full root control on underlying host servers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-112816 with a CVSS v4.0 score of 10.0, affects Canonical LXD container hypervisors and MicroCloud system deployments. The defect stems from improper validation of TLS client certificates during remote API authentication handshakes. An unauthenticated remote adversary with network access to the HTTPS management API and possession of a trusted client's public certificate can authenticate as that client without presenting the corresponding private key. Impersonating an administrative client grants full remote control over cluster virtual machines, storage pools, and host operating system root privileges.
Subverting cloud container hypervisors and cluster orchestration interfaces destroys tenant isolation and host security perimeters. Because LXD and MicroCloud manage production enterprise workloads and containerized microservices, unauthenticated administrative impersonation permits threat actors to deploy rogue virtual machines, access tenant memory spaces, and compromise core cloud infrastructure.
- Upgrade Canonical LXD and MicroCloud installations immediately to official vendor-supplied fixed software releases. - Restrict public network routing to LXD and MicroCloud HTTPS API interfaces, limiting access to isolated management VLANs. - Audit active TLS client certificate trust stores and revoke unverified client authentication entries. - Inspect cluster access logs and API call streams for anomalous administrative requests originating from unverified IP addresses.
Cloud container platform defense demands strict cryptographic authentication enforcement and rigid API control plane microsegmentation to ensure container hypervisors remain protected against unauthenticated client impersonation exploits. #CodeDefence #Canonical #LXD #MicroCloud #ContainerSecurity #CloudSecurity #RCE #AppSec #PatchManagement #DevSecOps

item.title: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero days CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 chained in wild attacks
item.description:
Perimeter remote access gateway maintainers have distributed security updates resolving two newly identified zero-day vulnerabilities actively weaponized in wild compromise campaigns. Unauthenticated remote adversaries chain authentication missing logic and predictable file path errors to execute arbitrary operating system commands under root privileges.
The security updates resolve Ivanti Connect Secure ICS vulnerabilities CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, which CISA added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under Binding Operational Directive 26-04. Threat intelligence disclosures from Volexity confirm threat group UTA0576 actively chained these flaws alongside authentication bypass zero-day CVE-2026-104935. By combining the three zero-days, adversaries bypassed security controls on fully patched appliances to deploy web shell backdoors, steal user credentials, exfiltrate internal configuration data, and alter event logs.
Subverting secure remote access gateways destroys perimeter boundary protections across corporate networks. Because Ivanti Connect Secure appliances manage single sign-on user sessions and SSL VPN tunnel terminations, an unauthenticated root takeover allows threat actors to intercept corporate network traffic, exfiltrate active session tokens, and move laterally across internal subnets.
- Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure appliances immediately to official maintenance release builds 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6. - Run the official Ivanti Integrity Checking Tool ICT to inspect local appliance filesystems for unauthorized web shell implants or modified binaries. - Isolate Ivanti management web interfaces behind zero trust access control proxies and enforce strict IP access control lists. - Invalidate active remote access user session tokens and execute mandatory administrative account password resets across managed appliances.
Perimeter gateway defense requires immediate patch application and continuous integrity validation to ensure secure remote access controllers remain shielded from unauthenticated root takeover chains. #CodeDefence #Ivanti #ConnectSecure #AuthBypass #CISA #KEV #ZeroDay #UTA0576 #NetworkSecurity #AppSec

item.title: Over 1000 Internet exposed GitLab instances remain unpatched against actively exploited RCE flaw CVE-2026-97229
item.description:
DevOps threat monitoring networks report significant global exposure following the passing of federal compliance patch deadlines. Security scans reveal over one thousand internet-exposed developer platform servers remaining unpatched against an actively exploited maximum-severity remote code execution vulnerability.
The ongoing threat activity targets self-hosted GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition instances vulnerable to integer overflow flaw CVE-2026-97229 carrying a CVSS score of 10.0. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed HTTP request parameters during pipeline execution handling to trigger integer wraparound memory corruption, achieving remote system command execution with elevated privileges on build runner nodes. Threat telemetry confirms automated botnet scanning arrays targeting exposed servers, including an incident where hackers attempted to compromise Alpine Linux development infrastructure.
Subverting central continuous integration build servers exposes enterprise software supply chains to malicious code injection and repository theft. Because self-hosted GitLab instances manage proprietary source code, container registry credentials, and deployment secrets, unauthenticated host exploitation allows threat actors to compromise software release artifacts and pivot into cloud environments.
- Apply official security updates released for GitLab CE and EE instances immediately across all self-hosted server deployments. - Restrict public internet routing to GitLab management interfaces and CI CD build runners using zero trust conditional access proxies. - Inspect CI CD build runner process execution logs for anomalous shell commands, unauthorized package installations, or unverified script invocations. - Rotate repository deployment keys, API integration tokens, and production cloud secrets configured within build runner environments.
Software development infrastructure security demands prompt dependency patch execution and strict build environment isolation to ensure continuous integration pipelines remain protected against unauthenticated command execution exploits. #CodeDefence #GitLab #DevSecOps #SupplyChain #RCE #CISA #KEV #AlpineLinux #AppSec #PatchManagement
